title: Choose the analytics layout
question: Which structure makes it easiest to scan operational health and investigate the details? All options keep the existing AssistDesk brand, filters, reports, audit history, and user directory.

options.label: Report Plate Index
options.thesis: A calm index sheet that turns each report area into a registered, clearly bounded plate.
options.viewport: Compact scope toolbar, a high-signal ticket summary, then aligned report plates with one line of registration detail at each section boundary.
options.risk: Can feel editorial unless the standard dashboard navigation and actions remain unmistakable.

options.label: Service Score
options.thesis: A time-and-state score makes ticket movement and department workload readable as one coordinated system.
options.viewport: Standard header and tabs above a wide departmental score: active load, resolved load, and response time align in rows; overview totals remain first.
options.risk: Dense rows may need careful labeling to avoid looking like an unfamiliar notation.

options.label: Live Metrics Specimen
options.thesis: One selected metric becomes the reading lens while every supporting chart updates its emphasis.
options.viewport: The top of Overview leads with a focused metric selector and oversized ticket total; priority, department, and resolution charts follow in a responsive grid.
options.risk: A focused metric must not hide the audit and record sections or make their filters ambiguous.
